current_activity: garrison cut off in Lorient; Fahrmbacher declines Kluge's order to take over Brest
notes: Event date: 7 August 1944 (Blumenson, ch. 18). Event definition: By 7 August land contact between Lorient and Brest has been cut; Fahrmbacher, in Lorient with the XXV Corps headquarters since 3 August, does not carry out the order to take command at Brest (Blumenson, ch. 18). Event support: one source family (the US Army official history (CMH)). Blumenson, Breakout and Pursuit, ch. 18, p. 343: "land contact between Lorient and Brest had already been cut". Location: Lorient, Morbihan with a precision of 5 km. Location support: Blumenson names Lorient. Commander: General Wilhelm Fahrmbacher, XXV Corps (Blumenson, ch. 18). Opponents: US 4th Armored Division. current_activity: garrison surrenders to the US 66th Infantry Division
notes: Event date: 10 May 1945 (MacDonald, ch. 20; Wikipedia). Event definition: The garrisons of Lorient and St. Nazaire surrender on 10 May to troops of the US 66th Infantry Division (MacDonald, ch. 20); the pocket held out nine months (Wikipedia, History of Lorient). Event support: two source families (the US Army official history (CMH), and Wikipedia). MacDonald, The Last Offensive, ch. 20, p. 477: "The garrisons of Lorient and St. Nazaire on the coast of Brittany surrendered on 10 May"; Wikipedia, History of Lorient: "The Lorient pocket held out against attack for nine months, before surrendering on May 10, 1945". Location: Lorient, Morbihan with a precision of 5 km. Location support: MacDonald and Wikipedia both name Lorient. Opponents: US 66th Infantry Division. Activity: garrison, span end, stated; in the activity pilot (October 2026) the old value of activity_status is blank, the new value is garrison (end, stated); reason: the surrender of the garrison ends its garrison role.
